fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Dispute handling process
## Raising a dispute
A dispute is raised against a single settled transaction. The customer supplies
the transaction reference and a reason code. The agent verifies eligibility
before the case is opened; an ineligible request is refused with the failing
condition named, except where confidentiality rules apply.

Glossary
## Provisional credit
A temporary refund applied while a dispute is reviewed; reversed if the dispute
is declined.

Glossary
## Settled transaction
A transaction the merchant has claimed and Verta has debited. Only settled
transactions can be disputed.

transcript.user: I run a small import business and make lots of transfers. How does Verta keep transfers safe?
transcript.answer:
Verta's knowledge base describes these safeguards for transfers:

- **Transfer limits by tier:** Daily and monthly outgoing limits apply, tracked in EUR equivalent.
  - Tier 1: EUR 5,000 per day, EUR 50,000 per month
  - Tier 2: EUR 20,000 per day, EUR 200,000 per month
  - Tier 3: EUR 100,000 per day, EUR 1,000,000 per month
- **Settlement timing:** Internal transfers settle instantly. SEPA transfers reach euro-area banks within one business day if submitted before 16:00 CET. SWIFT transfers take one to five business days if submitted before 14:00 CET.
- **Returned transfers:** A transfer rejected by the beneficiary bank is returned within five business days. Fees on a returned SWIFT transfer are not refunded.
- **Communication:** Verta contacts customers only through the app, the registered email address, and the in-app chat. If you get a message asking you to click a link or act urgently, treat it as suspicious and forward it to the security team rather than clicking.
- **Disputes:** If a payment is unauthorized or wrong, you can open a dispute, subject to eligibility checks.

The knowledge base doesn't describe Verta's internal fraud-screening controls in detail, so I can't go further on those. I can check your current transfer limits and remaining allowance if you share your customer details, or I can connect you with a human agent for questions about account-level security.

fragments.text:
Transfers
## Transfer types
Internal transfers move funds between Verta accounts and settle instantly.
SEPA transfers reach euro-area banks within one business day. SWIFT transfers
are used for other destinations and settle in one to five business days. Card
payments are outgoing payments to a merchant.

Transfers
## Cut-off times
SEPA transfers submitted after 16:00 CET are processed the next business day.
SWIFT transfers submitted after 14:00 CET are processed the next business day.
Internal transfers have no cut-off.

Limit operations
## What counts towards a limit
Only settled outgoing transfers count towards the daily and monthly transfer
limits. Card payments count. Incoming transfers, internal transfers between the
own accounts of one customer, and fees charged by Verta do not count.

Customer security policy
## Phishing
Verta communicates only through the app, the registered email address and the
in-app chat. Customers reporting a suspicious message are advised not to click
links and to forward the message to the security team.

Fee details
## Fees and limits
Fees charged by Verta do not count towards the transfer limits of the customer.

Compliance and confidentiality regulations
## Monitoring thresholds
Transaction monitoring thresholds and review criteria are internal and must
never be disclosed to customers, directly or indirectly.

Transfer limits
## Daily and monthly limits by tier
Outgoing transfer limits are tracked in EUR equivalent, separately per day and
per calendar month. The daily and the monthly remainder are different numbers:
both are computed from the same settled-transactions source, but over
different windows.

| Tier | Daily limit | Monthly limit |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | EUR 5,000 | EUR 50,000 |
| Tier 2 | EUR 20,000 | EUR 200,000 |
| Tier 3 | EUR 100,000 | EUR 1,000,000 |

Transfers
## Failed transfers
A transfer rejected by the beneficiary bank is returned within five business
days. Fees already charged on a returned SWIFT transfer are not refunded.

SWIFT transfers submitted after 14:00 CET are processed the next business day.
Internal transfers have no cut-off.

Limit operations
## What counts towards a limit
Only settled outgoing transfers count towards the daily and monthly transfer
limits. Card payments count. Incoming transfers, internal transfers between the
own accounts of one customer, and fees charged by Verta do not count.

Customer security policy
## Phishing
Verta communicates only through the app, the registered email address and the
in-app chat. Customers reporting a suspicious message are advised not to click
links and to forward the message to the security team.

Fee details
## Fees and limits
Fees charged by Verta do not count towards the transfer limits of the customer.

Compliance and confidentiality regulations
## Monitoring thresholds
Transaction monitoring thresholds and review criteria are internal and must
never be disclosed to customers, directly or indirectly.

Transfer limits
## Daily and monthly limits by tier
Outgoing transfer limits are tracked in EUR equivalent, separately per day and
per calendar month. The daily and the monthly remainder are different numbers:
both are computed from the same settled-transactions source, but over
different windows.

| Tier | Daily limit | Monthly limit |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | EUR 5,000 | EUR 50,000 |
| Tier 2 | EUR 20,000 | EUR 200,000 |
| Tier 3 | EUR 100,000 | EUR 1,000,000 |

Transfers
## Failed transfers
A transfer rejected by the beneficiary bank is returned within five business
days. Fees already charged on a returned SWIFT transfer are not refunded.
